antecedent_conditions: Two identical spaces S₁ and S₂ (same physical properties). Participants told S₁ was designed by a famous architect; S₂ by an unknown designer.
predicted_outcome:
- S₁ receives higher aesthetic ratings, longer viewing times, more positive affective report.
- Implicit measures (SCR, early ERP components) may or may not differ — the effect is primarily explicit.
- Under cognitive load, the attribution effect diminishes (Type 2 degraded → less explicit modulation).
- The effect is larger for ambiguous spaces (moderate quality) than for clearly excellent or clearly poor spaces.
expected_effect_sizes:
- Rating difference: d ≈ 0.3–0.5
- Load attenuation: d ≈ 0.2–0.4
- Ambiguity moderation: effect largest for moderate-quality spaces
architectural_test_case: Between-subjects: identical VR environments with different attributions. Within-subjects: cognitive load manipulation. Measure ratings, viewing time, SCR, EEG.
name: Placebo Architecture
